raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

DFLASH falls back to FlashInfer for targets outside the draft choices (such as `trtllm_mla`, `dsa`) and on SM110. FA4 is faster for GQA drafts on B200. The SM100 `trtllm_mha` fallback already uses FA4 and does not change.

## Modifications

On SM100 and SM110, the fallback returns FA4 for GQA drafts. MLA drafts keep FlashInfer, because FA4 fails at warmup unless `kv_lora_rank` is 512. Other GPUs, ROCm, XPU and explicit backends do not change.

- Fallback on SM100 and SM110 reads the draft config, and all resolver reads honor `--decrypted-draft-config-file`.
- FP8 targets whose draft moves to FA4 get a BF16 pool, even with explicit draft `fp8_e4m3`.
- Llama-3.1-8B does not move on B200, but pinned drafts on its FP8 FlashInfer target (page 64) give 1,015,680 target tokens on FlashInfer and 894,784 on FA4.
- The Kimi-K3 recipe now resolves to an unmeasured FA4 draft. With FP8, a reduced 6-layer dummy config at TP4 drops from 1,696,064 to 981,952 tokens (not representative).

Deliberate limits:

- A `head_dim` 256 GQA draft fails at warmup on FA4, where main uses FlashInfer. No public draft I checked uses 256.

These limits are deliberate. Do not add code for them without a real input that reaches the case.

## Accuracy Tests

Server runs used this head on B200.

Llama-3.1-8B on a FlashInfer target ran sgl-eval gsm8k (page 64, 200 examples, temperature 0, max tokens 1024, seed 0). FA4 drafts scored 81.50% and 82.00%, FlashInfer drafts 81.50%, 82.50% and 83.00%.

DFLASH unit tests on CPU and B200 fail only where main fails.

Not validated: SM90, SM110, B300, GB300, real Kimi-K3 or MLA drafts, Kimi-K3 with DCP, GLM-5.3-Flash serving on this head.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 at TP4 with cached 60K-token prompts ran on nightly `7224fce1` with this fallback, not this head.

| Streams | FlashInfer draft | FA4 draft | Gain |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 10.160 ms | 8.281 ms | 1.23x |
| 4 | 13.927 ms | 12.072 ms | 1.15x |
| 16 | 20.515 ms | 18.727 ms | 1.10x |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
